$comment: Retry with a budget, then escalate — openspec/changes/hydra-flows-first-port task 3.3.
The supervisor's `_auto_retry_or_escalate` + `_clear_auto_retry_labels`, as a
graph. A failing stage is retried up to `maxRetries` and then handed to a
human, and the OUTCOME LANDS ON THE ISSUE rather than only in a run log —
which is the half of the task that makes it useful to anyone not reading
flow runs.
🔑 The counter lives in FLOW STATE, keyed per flow, so it survives between
ticks (openregister#2216). A scheduled flow starts blank every run; without
this the budget would reset every time and 'retry twice' would mean 'retry
forever'.
⚠️ `bump` uses `compute`, not `set`. A template SUBSTITUTES and does not
CALCULATE — `{{retries}}` copies the counter and nothing could add one to
it. That is precisely why the first version of this flow retried forever
with the counter stuck at 0. openregister#2238 added `compute`.
Verified live with maxRetries=2:
fail -> retries 1     (retry)
fail -> retries 2     (retry)
fail -> retries 2     (budget exhausted; escalate, no bump)
pass -> counter gone  (cleared)
⚠️ The counter here is per FLOW, not per issue. That is correct for a
sequencer that handles one issue per tick and wrong if this graph is ever
reused for several issues at once — then the key has to include the issue
ref, and `flow-state` keys are literal, so it needs a `set-fields` step to
build the key first. Named because it will not announce itself.
🔑 `persist` AND `label-retry` USED TO SHARE ONE TOKEN, and only one of them
ever ran (REVALIDATION-2026-08-02 D3). Both were drawn `bumped → done`.
In a Petri net two transitions on one place COMPETE for its single token:
`FlowEngine::selectTransition()` takes the first unconditioned candidate,
which is `persist` by declaration order, `workflow->apply()` then moves the
token off `bumped`, and `label-retry` is never enabled again. It did not
appear in the run log at all across two retry cycles — no error, no warning,
and the counter advanced correctly the whole time, so the run looked right
while the issue was never told it was being retried.
Two steps that must BOTH happen are a SEQUENCE, not two edges out of one
place. `bumped → persist → persisted → label-retry → done` is the fix. A
genuine parallel split would be ONE transition with two `to` places; two
transitions with the same `from` is a choice, and the engine chooses.
name: Hydra retry and escalate
description: A failing stage is retried up to a budget and then escalated to a human, with the outcome written to the issue. Replaces hydra-supervisor.sh's _auto_retry_or_escalate. See openspec/changes/hydra-flows-first-port task 3.3.
